intro: A Portland choral-pop collective.
story: Ages and Ages are a Portland choral-pop collective who had played Pickathon in 2011 and came back in 2014, the year of Divisionary on Partisan. Tim Perry has kept the group going, and Fine Thanks and You was previewed ahead of its March 2026 release.
sets: Sat Aug 2, late night (1 am), Starlight Stage · Sun Aug 3, 11:20 am, Mountain View Stage

intro: A songwriter on the cusp of indie stardom.
story: Angel Olsen was on the cusp of indie-rock stardom when she played Pickathon in 2014, the year of Burn Your Fire for No Witness on Jagjaguwar. My Woman followed in 2016, All Mirrors in 2019 and Big Time in 2022, which the Americana Music Association nominated for Album of the Year. She has moved from stark folk-rock to sweeping orchestral pop and country-soul.
sets: Sat Aug 2, 6:30 pm, Lucky Barn · Sun Aug 3, 2:40 pm, Woods Stage

intro: Oregon's own indie-folk band.
story: Blind Pilot are an Oregon indie-folk band led by Israel Nebeker, already a Pacific Northwest staple when they played Pickathon in 2014. After eight years between records, they returned with In the Shadow of the Holy Mountain on ATO in 2024, and have toured it with a 2027 date booked in a Portland symphony hall.
sets: Fri Aug 1, 8:50 pm, Mountain View Stage · Sun Aug 3, 7:40 pm, Woods Stage

intro: A Dallas soul singer, songwriter and DJ.
story: Bobby Patterson is a Dallas soul singer, songwriter and longtime disc jockey who has worked since 1971, and in 2014 he brought decades of Texas R&B history to Pickathon. His last major studio album, I Got More Soul!, came out on Omnivore. There is no recent news.
sets: Fri Aug 1, 8 pm, Galaxy Barn · Sat Aug 2, 3:50 pm, Fir Meadows Stage

intro: An Austin Latin-funk band reinventing Black Sabbath.
story: Brownout are an Austin nine-piece Latin-funk band who played Pickathon in 2011 and again in 2014, with brass-heavy reinventions of Black Sabbath songs billed as Brown Sabbath. They remain an energetic fixture of Austin's live scene, and in 2026 played a hometown headline set for the Breakthrough Benefit Concert.
sets: Sat Aug 2, 8:40 pm, Fir Meadows Stage · Mon Aug 4, late night (1 am), Galaxy Barn

intro: A high-desert songwriter, back for a third visit.
story: Cahalen Morrison brought high-desert Americana and traditional string-band craft to Pickathon in 2011, 2013 and 2014. The New Mexico-bred songwriter has since spent five years living and writing in Scotland, and announced a new folk album, Broken Bell, for January 2027 on Hudson Records, with UK dates alongside Kris Drever.
sets: Fri Aug 1, 3 pm, Galaxy Barn · Sun Aug 3, 2 pm, Tree Line Stage

intro: A Minnesota resonator-guitar troubadour.
story: Charlie Parr plays resonator guitar with ferocious humility, and the Minnesota troubadour played Pickathon in 2011 and again in 2014. He has stayed on the road for years since, and was celebrated with a two-set career retrospective at the State Theatre in Minneapolis ahead of fall tour dates.
sets: Sat Aug 2, 12:30 pm, Lucky Barn · Sun Aug 3, 3:40 pm, Tree Line Stage

intro: An Australian songwriter, a year before the world caught on.
story: Courtney Barnett played Pickathon in 2014, the year before her breakthrough album, Sometimes I Sit and Think, and Sometimes I Just Sit, brought wide acclaim and a Brit Award nomination in 2016. Tell Me How You Really Feel followed in 2018 and Things Take Time, Take Time in 2021. She came back to headline in 2024, and her fourth album, Creature of Habit, written after a move to Los Angeles, was nominated for an ARIA Award in 2026.
sets: Sun Aug 3, 7:40 pm, Fir Meadows Stage · Sun Aug 3, 9:40 pm, Galaxy Barn

intro: A modern bluegrass band of fierce musicianship.
story: Della Mae are an all-women bluegrass band, led by Celia Woodsmith and Kimber Ludiker, who won the IBMA's New Artist of the Year in 2013 and were nominated for a Grammy for Best Bluegrass Album in 2014, the year they played Pickathon. They later made Magic Accident, produced by the banjoist Alison Brown.
sets: Sat Aug 2, 11 pm, Starlight Stage · Sun Aug 3, 12:30 pm, Lucky Barn

intro: Dan Bejar's unpredictable indie-rock institution.
story: Destroyer is Dan Bejar's band, an indie-rock institution since the 1990s, and they played Pickathon in 2014, three years after Kaputt on Merge. Poison Season followed in 2015 and Have We Met in 2020. Dan's Boogie, the fourteenth album, came out on Merge in 2025, and he toured with Father John Misty.
sets: Fri Aug 1, 4:20 pm, Woods Stage · Fri Aug 1, 7 pm, Tree Line Stage

intro: A four-guitar Nashville shred-fest.
story: Diarrhea Planet turned their 2014 Pickathon set into a joyful, four-guitar shred-fest. The Nashville band disbanded in 2018, reunited in November 2022, and still plays celebratory hometown shows, as at Marathon Music Works and Eastside Bowl.
sets: Sat Aug 2, late night (1 am), Galaxy Barn · Sat Aug 2, 4:20 pm, Woods Stage

intro: Eric D. Johnson, between Fruit Bats.
story: EDJ is Eric D. Johnson under his own initials, during a pause from Fruit Bats, when he played Pickathon in 2014. He has since reactivated Fruit Bats full-time, as a prolific songwriter and film scorer, and in the fall of 2026 he played a tour of more than thirty dates.
sets: Fri Aug 1, 5:20 pm, Tree Line Stage · Sun Aug 3, 4:40 pm, Galaxy Barn

intro: A theatrical psychedelic duo, back for a second year.
story: Foxygen are Sam France and Jonathan Rado, whose theatrical, 1960s-indebted psychedelic pop made 2013 a breakout year, the year they came to Pickathon, and they returned in 2014, the year of ...And Star Power on Jagjaguwar. Hang came in 2017. The duo stepped back from touring after Seeing Other People in 2019.
sets: Fri Aug 1, 11:20 pm, Galaxy Barn · Sun Aug 3, 6:20 pm, Mountain View Stage

intro: A Colorado farmer and songwriter of hushed, poetic folk.
story: Gregory Alan Isakov is a Colorado farmer and songwriter whose hushed, poetic folk songs made him a standout at Pickathon in 2014, a year after The Weatherman. Evening Machines, from 2018, was nominated for the Grammy for Best Folk Album, and Appaloosa Bones followed in 2023. He now plays with symphony orchestras and has opened for Zach Bryan at Gillette Stadium.
sets: Fri Aug 1, 6 pm, Woods Stage · Sat Aug 2, 6:10 pm, Fir Meadows Stage

intro: M.C. Taylor's soul-leaning folk band, on its first visit.
story: Hiss Golden Messenger arrived at Pickathon in 2014, the year of Lateness of Dancers on Merge, as M.C. Taylor's warm, soul-inflected folk-rock was finding a wider audience. They returned in 2015 and 2017. Terms of Surrender was nominated for the Grammy for Best Americana Album in 2021, and I'm People came on Chrysalis in 2026.
sets: Fri Aug 1, 3 pm, Fir Meadows Stage · Sun Aug 3, 3:30 pm, Lucky Barn

intro: A Portland band of jangly, laid-back guitar rock.
story: Houndstooth are a Portland band of jangly, laid-back guitar rock, who played Pickathon in 2014 a year after Ride Out the Dark. Their discography ends with No News from Home in 2015.
sets: Fri Aug 1, 3:40 pm, Tree Line Stage

intro: A founding Be Good Tanya turned nomadic songwriter.
story: Jolie Holland was a founding member of The Be Good Tanyas who launched her singular solo career early in the 2000s, and she played Pickathon in 2005, 2008 and again in 2014. She remains an uncompromising, nomadic songwriter, and in autumn 2026 she toured the Southwest, with stops in California, Arizona and New Mexico.
sets: Fri Aug 1, 6:30 pm, Mountain View Stage · Sun Aug 3, 1:20 pm, Galaxy Barn

intro: A punk and indie-rock original, here for the first of two visits.
story: Jonathan Richman began recording in the 1970s with the Modern Lovers, and he danced across Pickathon's stages in 2014, the year of No Me Quejo de Mi Estrella. He returned in 2017. He still tours small venues with drummer Tommy Larkins, and in 2025 released Only Frozen Sky Anyway on Blue Arrow.
sets: Sat Aug 2, 12:20 pm, Mountain View Stage · Sun Aug 3, 10 pm, Starlight Stage

intro: A wordless looped-voice composer.
story: Julianna Barwick made wordless, looped vocal cathedrals that felt tailor-made for the woods when she played Pickathon in 2014, after The Magic Place in 2011 and Nepenthe in 2013. Will followed in 2016 and Healing Is a Miracle in 2020. She has since teamed with the harpist Mary Lattimore on Tragic Magic for InFiné.
sets: Sat Aug 2, 3:30 pm, Lucky Barn · Sun Aug 3, 5:20 pm, Tree Line Stage

intro: A Louisiana accordionist of Creole dance-floor energy.
story: Leroy Thomas is a Louisiana accordionist who brought infectious Creole dance-floor energy to Pickathon in 2014, with the Zydeco Roadrunners. He remains a dependable standard-bearer of classic zydeco in Acadiana, performing at venues like Vermilionville in Lafayette.
sets: Fri Aug 1, 1:50 pm, Mountain View Stage · Sat Aug 2, 12:20 pm, Tree Line Stage

intro: A late-blooming improviser and sculptor.
story: Lonnie Holley is an Alabama artist whose found-object sculptures and sprawling, intuitive songs felt like dispatches from another realm when he played Pickathon in 2014, and he came back in 2018, the year of MITH on Jagjaguwar. Oh Me Oh My followed in 2023 and Tonky in 2025. In August 2026 he played Seattle's Neptune Theatre with Bill Callahan, and then the Brooklyn Folk Festival.
sets: Fri Aug 1, 2:40 pm, Woods Stage · Sun Aug 3, 2 pm, Lucky Barn

intro: A Northwest indie-rock band of scruffy melodies.
story: Love As Laughter was Sam Jayne's Northwest indie-rock band, and left a catalog of scruffy, melodic records such as Laughter's Fifth on Sub Pop in 2005. Writers and fans still celebrate the late Sam Jayne.
sets: Fri Aug 1, 12:40 pm, Fir Meadows Stage · Sat Aug 2, 3 pm, Galaxy Barn

intro: A tape-warped slacker-pop songwriter, just spreading beyond DIY.
story: Mac DeMarco hit Pickathon in 2014, the year of Salad Days on Captured Tracks, which the Polaris Prize shortlisted, and his gap-toothed grin and jangly slacker pop were just beginning to travel beyond DIY circles. A Juno nomination for Breakthrough Artist came in 2015, and he returned in 2016. He has since gone quieter, with home recordings and, in November 2026, a tour of Mexico.
sets: Sat Aug 2, 7:40 pm, Woods Stage · Sun Aug 3, 11:30 pm, Starlight Stage

intro: A North Carolina duo, here for the first of five visits.
story: Mandolin Orange are Andrew Marlin and Emily Frantz, whose close harmonies and unhurried acoustic storytelling won listeners over at Pickathon in 2014. They returned in 2015, 2017, 2019 and 2023, and renamed themselves Watchhouse in 2021. Rituals came out on Thirty Tigers in 2025.
sets: Sat Aug 2, 2 pm, Lucky Barn · Sun Aug 3, 7 pm, Tree Line Stage

intro: A keyboardist of groove-heavy piano experiments.
story: Marco Benevento is a keyboardist who brought joyful, groove-heavy piano experiments to Pickathon in 2013 and again in 2014. He is now a fixture of the Hudson Valley scene, and released Glera on Big Crown Records in 2026 and hosted the fifth year of his Follow the Arrow Festival.
sets: Sun Aug 3, late night (1 am), Galaxy Barn · Sun Aug 3, 5:10 pm, Fir Meadows Stage

intro: A garage-rock and baroque-pop songwriter.
story: Mikal Cronin was known in 2014 for pairing garage-rock fuzz with baroque pop hooks, alongside his frequent collaborator Ty Segall, a year after MCII on Merge. Seeker came out in 2019, and he played East Coast club dates in the spring of 2026.
sets: Sat Aug 2, 1:30 pm, Fir Meadows Stage · Sun Aug 3, 3 pm, Galaxy Barn

intro: Bluegrass trailblazers, between hiatuses.
story: Nickel Creek are Chris Thile, Sara Watkins and Sean Watkins, who had won the IBMA's New Artist of the Year in 2000 and a Grammy for Best Contemporary Folk Album in 2003, and who played Pickathon in 2014, the year of A Dotted Line on Nonesuch. That album drew a Grammy nomination for Best Americana Album. They ended a long hiatus with Celebrants in 2023 and an extended reunion tour.
sets: Sat Aug 2, 1 pm, Woods Stage · Sat Aug 2, 9:50 pm, Mountain View Stage

intro: An Appalachian fiddle and banjo band.
story: Old Buck brought deep-rooted Appalachian fiddle and banjo traditions to Pickathon in 2014, with acclaimed old-time musicians including Riley Baugus, and played the festival's square dance with caller Caroline Oakley. There is no recent news.
sets: Fri Aug 1, 2 pm, Tree Line Stage · Sun Aug 3, 5 pm, Lucky Barn

intro: Dan Boeckner's urgent synth-driven post-punk.
story: Operators are Dan Boeckner's synth-driven post-punk band, from the singer of Wolf Parade and Divine Fits, and they played Pickathon in 2014. Blue Wave came out on Last Gang in 2016 and Radiant Dawn in 2019, and Boeckner has since put out his own solo work.
sets: Sat Aug 2, 5 pm, Mountain View Stage · Sun Aug 3, 6:20 pm, Galaxy Barn

intro: A wired, deadpan post-punk band, back after 2013.
story: Parquet Courts tore through Pickathon in 2013 and returned in 2014, the year of Sunbathing Animal. Human Performance followed in 2016, its packaging nominated for a Grammy, Wide Awake in 2018 and Sympathy for Life in 2021. With the band quiet since, co-frontman Andrew Savage announced a new band, Iconic Fugues, with European dates in 2027.
sets: Sun Aug 3, 6 pm, Woods Stage

intro: An underground hip-hop duo of crate-dug beats.
story: People Under the Stairs are Thes One and Double K of Los Angeles, underground hip-hop favorites on crate-dug beats and easygoing camaraderie who played Pickathon in 2014. They retired in 2019, and Thes One has gone on producing, lecturing and releasing archival material, among it Project 1992.
sets: Sat Aug 2, 6 pm, Woods Stage · Sun Aug 3, 8 pm, Galaxy Barn

intro: A one-man band of sweat-drenched catharsis.
story: Possessed by Paul James is Konrad Wert, a one-man band who stomped and sawed his fiddle through Pickathon in 2014 like his life depended on it. He balances life on the road with work as a special education teacher in Texas, and in fall 2026 toured the United Kingdom, Europe and the American Northeast and Midwest.
sets: Fri Aug 1, 6:30 pm, Lucky Barn · Sat Aug 2, 1:20 pm, Galaxy Barn

intro: A Boston psych-folk quartet of sunlit harmonies.
story: Quilt are a Boston psych-folk quartet who brought sunlit harmonies and hazy guitar interplay to Pickathon in 2014. Plaza came out on Mexican Summer in 2016. The band has been inactive since the late 2010s, and co-founder Anna Fox Rochinski plays in New York.
sets: Sat Aug 2, 2 pm, Tree Line Stage · Sun Aug 3, 11:40 am, Galaxy Barn

intro: An alt-country mainstay with wit and bluegrass chops.
story: Robbie Fulks had been an alt-country mainstay since Country Love Songs on Bloodshot in 1996, and he brought sharp wit and bluegrass chops to Pickathon in 2014. Upland Stories, in 2016, drew Grammy nominations for Best Contemporary Folk Album and, for Alabama at Night, Best American Roots Song. Now Then came on Compass in 2025, and in November 2026 he toured the Northeast and Pacific Northwest, with dates alongside the fiddler Jenny Scheinman.
sets: Fri Aug 1, 4:10 pm, Mountain View Stage · Sat Aug 2, 7 pm, Tree Line Stage

intro: A one-man band with a suitcase drum, back for a second year.
story: Shakey Graves is Alejandro Rose-Garcia, the Austin one-man band who kicked a suitcase drum and howled folk-blues at Pickathon in 2013, and who came back in 2014, the year before the Americana Music Association named him Emerging Act of the Year. And the War Came was nominated for Album of the Year. He returned in 2018 and 2026, and his May 2026 album, Fondness, Etc., came with Texas dates in November.
sets: Fri Aug 1, 7:40 pm, Fir Meadows Stage · Sun Aug 3, 4:20 pm, Woods Stage

intro: A smoky blues and soul singer.
story: Son Little is Aaron Livingston, whose smoky, genre-blurring blues and soul felt timeless and fresh when he played Pickathon in 2014. New Magic came out on Anti- in 2017 and aloha in 2020. After a quiet stretch he returned in early 2026 with the single In Orbit and a long North American and European tour.
sets: Sat Aug 2, 5:20 pm, Tree Line Stage · Sun Aug 3, 6:30 pm, Lucky Barn

intro: A psych-soul trio from three bands.
story: Spanish Gold was formed by Patrick Hallahan of My Morning Jacket, Adrian Quesada and Dante Schwebel, and brought psych-tinged soul-rock to Pickathon in 2014 behind their one album, South of Nowhere. There is no recent news.
sets: Sat Aug 2, 6:20 pm, Galaxy Barn · Sun Aug 3, 1:40 pm, Mountain View Stage

intro: A fingerpicking guitarist whose solo career was taking off.
story: Steve Gunn brought hypnotic, fingerpicked folk-rock to Pickathon in 2014, the year of Way Out Weather on Paradise of Bachelors, just as his solo career was taking off. He returned in 2017. Eyes on the Lines came on Matador in 2016, then The Unseen In Between and Other You, and Daylight Daylight on No Quarter in 2025. In fall 2026 he played New York, Massachusetts and California, including a show with Bridget St John.
sets: Fri Aug 1, 5 pm, Lucky Barn · Sun Aug 3, late night (12:30 am), Starlight Stage

intro: A harp-laced Montreal band, back after 2012.
story: The Barr Brothers are a harp-laced Montreal band who stood out at Pickathon in 2012, and returned in 2014. The Polaris Prize long-listed them three times, in 2012, 2015 and 2018, for the last with Queens of the Breakers, which also drew a Juno nomination. They toured their fourth album, Let It Hiss.
sets: Fri Aug 1, 9:40 pm, Galaxy Barn · Sun Aug 3, 4 pm, Mountain View Stage

intro: A Knoxville band of soulful, jam-friendly Americana.
story: The Black Lillies are a Knoxville band led by Cruz Contreras who played Pickathon in 2010, 2011 and 2014, after Runaway Freeway Blues in 2013. They have logged countless miles across festivals and stages, and closed 2026 with a New Year's Eve show at The Down Home in Johnson City, Tennessee.
sets: Fri Aug 1, 6:20 pm, Galaxy Barn · Sat Aug 2, 11:10 am, Fir Meadows Stage

intro: A Port Townsend jug and string-band duo.
story: The Crow Quill Night Owls are a Port Townsend, Washington band who brought ragtime, jug band and pre-war string-band stomp to Pickathon in 2014. There is no recent news.
sets: Fri Aug 1, 3:30 pm, Lucky Barn · Sun Aug 3, 12:20 pm, Tree Line Stage

intro: A San Diego band of sun-bleached coastal rock.
story: The Donkeys are a San Diego band of breezy, sun-bleached coastal rock in the California-harmony tradition, who played Pickathon in 2014. They are still at it, and in July 2025 released La danza dei Serpenti.
sets: Fri Aug 1, 7:40 pm, Woods Stage

intro: A Portland honky-tonk duo.
story: The Earnest Lovers are the Portland honky-tonk duo of Pete Krebs and Leslie Beia, who brought classic country heartbreak and crisp acoustic picking to Pickathon in 2014. Krebs remains a longtime fixture of the Portland scene.

intro: A Brooklyn band of shapeshifting punk.
story: The Men are a Brooklyn band whose shapeshifting punk, between noise-rock and heartland grit, tore through Pickathon in 2014, the year of Tomorrow's Hits on Sacred Bones and two years after Open Your Heart. They have stayed fiercely independent, on the UK label Fuzz Club with New York City in 2023 and Buyer Beware in 2025.
sets: Sat Aug 2, 8 pm, Galaxy Barn · Sun Aug 3, 2:50 pm, Fir Meadows Stage

intro: Canadian psych-country road warriors, back for a third visit.
story: The Sadies had played Pickathon in 2009 and 2011 before they came back in 2014, the year of Internal Sounds, which the Polaris Prize long-listed. After Northern Passages in 2017, Colder Streams on Yep Roc in 2022 made the Polaris short list in 2023. Dallas Good died in 2022, and the remaining members have gone on touring and released Live at 6 O'Clock, with Gord Downie.
sets: Sat Aug 2, 11:20 pm, Galaxy Barn · Sun Aug 3, 12:30 pm, Fir Meadows Stage

intro: An indie-rock band just before their breakthrough.
story: The War on Drugs had played Pickathon in 2012 and returned in 2014, the year of Lost in the Dream on Secretly Canadian. A Deeper Understanding, on Atlantic in 2017, won the Grammy for Best Rock Album in 2018. Adam Granduciel's widescreen rock now fills major stages, including Austin City Limits in fall 2026.
sets: Fri Aug 1, 9:20 pm, Woods Stage · Sat Aug 2, 9:40 pm, Galaxy Barn

intro: A rowdy Nashville country-punk band.
story: Those Darlins were a Nashville band of rowdy, garage-infused country punk who played Pickathon in 2014 and disbanded in 2016. Their records carry the spirit of the late Jessi Zazu, and former members remain active in Nashville.
sets: Fri Aug 1, 4:40 pm, Galaxy Barn · Sat Aug 2, 3:40 pm, Tree Line Stage

intro: Ruban Nielson's warped psychedelic funk, just before breaking out.
story: Unknown Mortal Orchestra are Ruban Nielson's Portland-rooted project, whose warped, lo-fi psychedelic funk came to Pickathon in 2014 a year after II on Jagjaguwar. Multi-Love followed in 2015, Sex & Food in 2018 and V in 2023. In 2026 he released the Sabbath-tinged EP Curse, channeling grief into heavy riffs.
sets: Sat Aug 2, 2:40 pm, Mountain View Stage · Sun Aug 3, 11:20 pm, Galaxy Barn

intro: A Portland soul veteran with a late-career revival.
story: Ural Thomas is a Portland soul singer who brought decades of classic R&B showmanship to Pickathon in 2014, after a remarkable late-career revival with his band the Pain. He is still beloved at home, and in July 2026 headlined a Sunday evening at the Washington Park Summer Festival.
sets: Fri Aug 1, 5:20 pm, Fir Meadows Stage · Sat Aug 2, 11:40 am, Galaxy Barn

intro: A singular voice with an organic moonshine roots sound.
story: Valerie June arrived at Pickathon in 2014, the year after Pushin' Against a Stone on Concord, with an unmistakable voice and what she calls an organic moonshine roots sound. The Americana Music Association nominated her as an emerging act that year. The Order of Time came in 2017 and The Moon and Stars in 2021, which drew a Grammy nomination, and she returned to the farm in 2022.
sets: Fri Aug 1, 11:30 pm, Starlight Stage · Sat Aug 2, 2:40 pm, Woods Stage

intro: A Los Angeles art-rock quartet of hypnotic interplay.
story: Warpaint are a Los Angeles quartet whose hypnotic, rhythmic art-rock gained wider attention when they played Pickathon in 2014, the year of their self-titled album on Rough Trade. Heads Up followed in 2016 and Radiate Like This in 2022, their last album, which they celebrated with an anniversary.
sets: Sat Aug 2, 7:20 pm, Mountain View Stage · Sun Aug 3, 9:20 pm, Woods Stage

intro: A former Old Crow Medicine Show singer, solo and old-time.
story: Willie Watson, formerly of Old Crow Medicine Show, played Pickathon in 2014 as a solo folk revivalist steeped in old-time ballads, the year of Folk Singer, Vol. 1. He released a self-titled album of original songs in late 2024.
sets: Sat Aug 2, 5 pm, Lucky Barn · Mon Aug 4, late night (1 am), Starlight Stage

intro: A Brooklyn folk-rock band with tape-hissed jams.
story: Woods are a Brooklyn band who brought warm, tape-hissed folk-rock and extended jams to Pickathon in 2014, while running their influential label, Woodsist. Their last studio album, Perennial, came out in 2023.
sets: Sat Aug 2, 4:40 pm, Galaxy Barn · Sun Aug 3, 1 pm, Woods Stage

intro: Los Angeles punk pioneers, by then elder statesmen.
story: X are John Doe, Exene Cervenka, Billy Zoom and D.J. Bonebrake, the Los Angeles punk pioneers behind Los Angeles on Slash in 1980, and they came to Pickathon in 2014. Alphabetland came in 2020 and Smoke & Fiction, billed as their final studio album, in 2024.
sets: Sat Aug 2, 9:20 pm, Woods Stage · Sun Aug 3, 8:50 pm, Mountain View Stage
